# Judith Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_004_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The Israelites living in Judea heard everything that Holofernes, the chief commander of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians, had done to the nations, and how he had plundered all their temples and handed them over to destruction.

**2** They were greatly afraid before him and trembled for Jerusalem and for the temple of the Lord their God.

**3** For they had only recently returned from captivity, and all the people of Judea had just been gathered together again, and the vessels and the altar and the house had just been reconsecrated after their defilement.

**4** So they sent word throughout all the territory of Samaria and Kona and Beth-horon and Belmain and Jericho and to Choba and Aesora and to the valley of Salem.

**5** They seized the heights of the high mountains in advance, fortified the villages in them, and stored up provisions in preparation for war, since their fields had just been harvested.

**6** Joakim the high priest, who was in Jerusalem at that time, wrote to those dwelling in Bethulia and Betomesthaim, which is opposite Esdraelon facing the plain near Dothan,

**7** ordering them to seize the passes through the hill country in advance, since these were the gateways into Judea and it would be easy to hold off those advancing — the approach was so narrow that only two men could pass through together.

**8** The Israelites did exactly as Joakim the high priest had commanded them, and as the council of all the people of Israel assembled in Jerusalem had directed.

**9** Every man in Israel cried out to God with great fervor, and they humbled themselves before him with great earnestness.

**10** They — along with their wives and their children and their cattle and every resident alien and hired worker and slave purchased with their money — girded sackcloth on their loins.

**11** Every man and woman and young child living in Jerusalem fell prostrate before the temple, put ashes on their heads, and spread out their sackcloth before the Lord.

**12** They also wrapped the altar in sackcloth and cried out with one voice in great fervor to the God of Israel not to give their infants as plunder and their wives as spoil and the cities of their inheritance to destruction and the sanctuary to desecration and disgrace — not to make it a reproach for the nations.

**13** The Lord heard their voice and looked upon their affliction. The people fasted for many days throughout all Judea and in Jerusalem before the sanctuary of the Lord Almighty.

**14** Joakim the high priest and all the priests who served before the Lord and ministered to him wore sackcloth girded around their loins while they offered the daily burnt offering and the votive offerings and the freewill offerings of the people.

**15** They had ashes on their turbans, and they cried out to the Lord with all their strength, asking that he look with favor on the whole house of Israel.
